m: विट् (prob. artificial; cf. √ बिट् and विड्) cl. 1. P. वेटति, to sound, Dhātup. ix, 29.
1. विट् (for 2. See p. 995, col. 2), in comp. for 2. विश्.
2. विट् (for 1. See p. 989, col. 2) in comp. for 3. विष्.
a: विट् — {c1c} P. (वेटति) 1 To sound. --2 To curse, rail at.

m: विटाश्रय m. a house occupied by a Viṭa, L.
विटाटिका f. (?) a kind of small hog-weed, L.
a room where Viṭas meet, L.

m: विट्—खदिर m. Vachellia Farnesiana, L.

k.v: अरिमेदो विट्खदिरे कदरः खदिरे सिते। सोमवल्कोऽप्यथ व्याघ्रपुच्छगन्धर्वहस्तकौ॥

m: विट्—शूद्र n. sg. Vaiśyas and Śūdras, R.
विट्—शूल m. a partic. form of colic, Suśr.
विट्ठलाचार्य-सूनु m. N. of a Commentator, Cat.
विट्ठलाष्टोत्तर-शत n. N. of a Stotra.
विट्ठली-पद्धति f. N. of an astron. wk. by Viṭṭhalācārya.

विट्ठल m. (also written विठल, विठ्ठल, and विढ्ढल) N. of a god worshipped at Pandharpur in the Deccan (he is commonly called Viṭho-bā, and stated to be an incarnation of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa himself, who is believed to have visited this city and infused a large portion of his essence into a Brāhman named Puṇḍarīka or Puṇḍalīka, who had gained a great reputation for filial piety; his images represent him standing on a brick [cf. 2. विड्] with his arms akimbo), RTL. 263

(also with आचार्य, दीक्षित, भट्ट &c.) N. of various authors and teachers (esp. of a grammarian, disparaged by Bhaṭṭoji, and of a son of Vallabhācārya and successor to his chair, also called Viṭṭhala-dīkṣita or Viṭṭhala-nātha or Viṭṭhaleśa or Viṭṭhaleśvara, said to have been born in 1515), Cat.
a: विट्ठ(ठ्ठ)लः — N. of a form of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa (worshipped at Pandharpur in the Bombay presidency).

m: विट्ठल—कवच n. N. of a Kavaca (q.v.)
विट्ठल—मिश्र m. N. of a Commentator, Cat.
विट्ठल—सूनु m. N. of an author, Cat.
विट्ठल—सहस्र-नामन् n. N. of wk.
विट्ठल—स्तव-राज m. N. of wk.
विट्ठलेश or ˚लेश्वर, see above.
विट्ठलोपाध्याय-पत्त्र n. N. of wk.

puM, (vewatIti । viwa + kaH .) ziqgaH । ityamaraH ॥ (yaTA, BAgavate । 10 । 13 । 2 । “satAmayaM sAraBftAM nisargo yadarTavARISruticetasAmapi । pratikzaRaM navyavadacyutasya yat striyA viwAnAmiva sADu vArttA ॥”) kAmukAnucaraH । DUrttaH । iti BarataH ॥ kAmatandrakalAkovidaH । iti rasamaYjarI ॥ parvvataviSezaH । lavaRaBedaH । KadiraviSezaH । mUzikaH । iti medinI । we, 28 ॥ nAraNgavfkzaH । iti SabdamAlA ॥

m: विट m. (derivation doubtful) a voluptuary, sensualist, bon-vivant, boon-companion, rogue, knave, Kāv.; Rājat.; Kathās. &c. (in the drama, esp. in the Mṛcchakaṭikā, he is the companion of a dissolute prince and resembles in some respects the Vidūṣaka, being generally represented as a parasite on familiar terms with his associate, but at the same time accomplished in the arts of poetry, music, and singing; ifc. a term of reproach g. खसूच्य्-आदि, Gaṇar.; L. also ‘the keeper of a prostitute; a catamite; a mouse; Acacia Catechu; the orange tree; a kind of salt; = प्राञ्चल्लोह [?]; = विटप N. of a mountain’)
विट n. a house, Gal.
a: विटः — [विट्-क] 1 A paramour; त्वद्वत्सलः क्व स तपस्विजनस्य हंता कन्याविटः पतिरसौ परिरक्षतु त्वां Māl. 8. 8; Śi. 4. 48. --2 A voluptuary, sensualist. --3 (In dramas) The companion of a prince or dissolute young man, or of a courtezan (who is described as being skilled in the arts of singing, music, and poetry and as a parasite on familiar terms with his associate to whom he nearly serves the purpose of the Vidūṣaka; see inter alia Mk. acts 1, 5, and 8); for definition, see S. D. 78. --4 A rogue, cheat. --5 A catamite. --6 A rat. --7 The Khadira tree. --8 The orange tree. --9 A branch together with its shoot. --10 A mineral salt. --Comp. --माक्षिकं a kind of mineral. --लवणं a medicinal salt.

m: विट—भूत m. N. of an Asura, MBh.

a: विटंकः — 1 An aviary, dove-cot. --2 The loftiest point, pinnacle, elevation; अयमेव महीधरविटंकः Māl. 10; Vikr. 5. 77.

s: puM klI, (viSezeRawaNkyate sODAdizu iti । vi + waNka banDane + GaY .) kapotapAlikA । pAyavAra Kopa iti BAzA । ityamaraH ॥ dve sODAdizu prAnte kAzWAdiracite gfhapakzisTAne । kapotAn pAlayatIti kapotapAlI QAt zaR iti zaR svArTe kaH kapota ityupalakzaRaM pakzimAtrapAliketi boDyam । vIn pakziRazwaNkayati baDnAti viwaNkaM waki ka banDe zaR viSezeRa waNkayatyatreti vA al GaY vA । iti BarataH ॥ (yaTA, mAGe । 3 । 55 । “ratAntare yatra gfhAntarezu vitarddiniryUhaviwaNkanIqaH । rutAni SfRvan vayasAM gaRo'ntevAsitvamApa sPuwamaNganAnAm ॥” * ॥ sundare, tri । yaTA, BAgavate । 3 । 15 । 27 । “devAvacakzata gfhItagadO parArddyakeyUrakuRqalakirIwaviwaNkaveSO ॥”)
v: na॰ vi + waki--ac । kapotapAlikAyAM prAsAdAdyagrasTe kAzWanirmite kapotAvAsasTAne । (pAyarAKopa) amaraH ।
m: वि-टङ्क m. n. (g. अर्धर्चादि; see √ टङ्क् and टङ्क) the loftiest point, top, pinnacle, MBh.; Kāv. &c. (also ˚कक, L.)
a dove-cot, aviary, L.
वि-टङ्क m. a big cucumber, L.
वि-टङ्क mfn. trim, nice, pretty, handsome, Pracaṇḍ.; BhP.

k.v: गोपानसी तु वलभी छादने वक्रदारुणि। कपोतपालिकायां तु विटङ्कं पुन्नपुंसकम्.।

s: puM klI, (viwaNka eva । svArTe kan .) viwaNkaH । iti SabdaratnAvalI ॥

m: वि-टङ्क—पुर n. N. of a town, Kathās.
वि-˚टङ्कित mfn. stamped or marked or adorned with (instr. or comp.), BhP.
विटका f. a room where Viṭas meet.
विट—कान्ता f. turmeric, L.
विटक m. pl. N. of a people, VarBṛS.
= पिटक, a boil, blister, Gal.
विट—लवण n. a kind of salt (= विड्-ल्˚), L.

SAKApallavasamudAyaH । tatparyyAyaH । vistAraH 2 । ityamaraH ॥ stambaH 3 । iti medinI । pe, 22 ॥ SAKA । (yaTA, raGuH । 10 । 11 । “bAhuBirviwapAkArErdivyABaraRaBUzitEH । AvirBUtamapAM maDye pArijAtamivAparam ॥”) pallavaH । iti SabdaratnAvalI ॥ (yaTA, ftusaMhAre । 1 । 24 । “taruviwapalatAgrAliNganavyAkulena diSi diSi paridagDA BUmayaH pAvakena ॥”) klI, muzkavaNkzaRAntaram । yaTA, -- “viwapantu mahAbIjyamantarAmuzkavaNkzaRam ॥” iti hemacandraH ॥ (yaTA, suSrute । 3 । 6 । “vaNkzaRavfzaRayorantare viwapaM nAma tatra zARwyamalpaSukratA vA Bavati ॥”)

m: 1. विट—प m. (for 2. See below) a keeper of catamites, L.
2. विटप m. n. (g. अर्धर्चादि; of doubtful derivation accord. to Uṇ. iii, 145 fr. √ विट्; for 1. विट-प See under विट), the young branch of a tree or creeper, twig, sprout, shoot, bough, MBh.; Kāv. &c.
a bush, shrub, cluster, thicket, tuft, ib.
expansion, spreading, L.
the perinaeum or the septum of the scrotum, Suśr.
विटप m. N. of a man g. शिवादि = विट or विटाधिप, L.
a: विटपः — [विटं विस्तारं वा पाति पिबति पा˚ क Tv.] 1 A branch, bough (of a creeper or tree); कोमलविटपानुकारिणौ बाहू Ś. 1. 21, 32; यदनेन तरुर्त पातितः क्षपिता तद्विटपाश्रिता लता R. 8. 47; Śi. 4. 48; Ku. 6. 41. --2 A bush. --3 A new shoot or sprout; Śi. 7. 53. --4 A cluster, clump, thicket. --5 Extension. --6 The septum of the scrotum.

k.v: पत्रं पलाशं छदनं दलं पर्णं छदः पुमान्. पल्लवोऽस्त्री किसलयं विस्तारो विटपोऽस्त्रियाम्.।
तल्पं शय्याट्टदारेषु स्तम्बेऽपि विटपोऽस्त्रियाम्. प्राप्तरूपस्वरूपाभिरूपा बुधमनोज्ञयोः॥

m: विटप—शस् ind. in branches or shoots, BhP.
विटपक m. a tree, Kād.
a rogue, voluptuary (= विट), ib.
विट—पेटक m. or n. a multitude of rogues, Rājat.
विटपि-मृग m. ‘tree-animal’, a monkey, ape, MW.

m: विटपिन् mfn. having branches or boughs (as a tree), MBh.

the Indian fig-tree, L.
a: विटपिन् — m. [विटप-अस्त्यर्थे इनि] 1 A tree; परितो दृष्टाश्च विटपिनः सर्वे Bv. 1. 21, 29. --2 The fig-tree. --Comp. --मृगः a monkey, an ape.

m: विट—प्रिय m. a kind of jasmine, L.

विट—वल्लभा f. Bignonia Suaveolens, L.
विट—वृत्त m. N. of a poet, Cat.

m: विट्—कारिका f. ‘ordure maker’, a kind of bird (prob. a variety of Turdus Salica), L.

विट्क (ifc.) = 3. विष्, feces (cf. कर्ण- and भिन्न-विट्क).

a chief of Vaiśyas, BhP.
a daughter's husband, son-in-law, Mn. iii, 148
a head-merchant, W.
